Odesa First Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Odes'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Odessa's First Jewish cemetery, established in the late 18th century, was the earlier of the city's two 19th-into-20th-century Jewish burial grounds — it closed in 1912, decades before its counterpart (the Second Jewish Cemetery), and was destroyed by Soviet authorities in 1935, then completely leveled again during WWII and built over. It served the same enormous Jewish community that once numbered nearly 139,000 people by 1897 and endured the loss of over 40,000 people in a single wave of massacres in October 1941. A school, a swimming pool, a gym, and a car wash now occupy the former cemetery grounds.
